text:
Ana (Docs): Hi team — opened a docs PR to update the model catalog + model card for redwood/mistral-7b. Main changes: mark redwood/mistral-quant-v1 as deprecated, add supported limits (context, tokens), include benchmark table, and add an SDK migration snippet. PTAL @Sam (ML) @Zack (SDK) @Devon (Runtime). PR: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/pull/462

docs-bot: PR opened: #462 — docs/model-catalog: update mistral-7b model card (Ana (Docs))

Sam (ML): Thanks — looks good. Can you include micro/throughput numbers at 512 and 2048 contexts? I ran a quick local bench on A100-80GB with kv-cache warm:
```
512 tokens: 7.3 ms/token (avg), 1800 tok/s
2048 tokens: 9.8 ms/token (avg), 1020 tok/s
Peak memory (512): 9.6 GB
Peak memory (2048): 18.2 GB
```
I'll attach raw CSV to the PR comment. Also note quant variant shows +12% latency when the fallback float path kicks in.

Devon (Runtime): Important compatibility note: the quantized build currently doesn't support grouped-gemm optimizations on some kernels — that causes fallback to float execution for some layers. Please add a "Compatibility" section stating:
- "Quantized variants may fall back to float kernels on older CUDA/driver combos (>=11.7 recommended). This increases memory and latency; we recommend the non-quant model for Dedicated with continuous_batching enabled until runtime fix #789 ships."
Also mention: if you see OOMs with continuous batching, runtime will fall back to single-request paths; include the log snippet users will see.

Zack (SDK): Dropped an SDK snippet in the PR comments. Example Python migration (using new model_version param and structured response):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()
resp = client.generate(
    model="redwood/mistral-7b",
    model_version="2026-02-15",
    prompt="Summarize the document",
    max_tokens=256,
    response_format="text"
)
print(resp.output_text)
```
Note: recommend using model_version pinned values for reproducible results. I'll also add a TypeScript snippet if you want.

Maria (Product): A couple product asks: make the limits explicit in the card — max context 8192 tokens (soft recommend 4096 for <50ms/token latency), max request rate for hosted tier: soft throttle at 150 RPS/model, and include per-tier benchmark table (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Can we add a small row for expected cost per 1k tokens for each variant? If not exact numbers, at least relative buckets (low/medium/high).

Ana (Docs): Good calls — I'll add a "Limits" subsection and a small benchmark table. @Zack please add TS sample under "SDK examples" and @Sam can you attach the CSV and a short sentence about how you ran the bench (batch size, concurrency). I'll add the compatibility language Devon suggested and a brief migration checklist for customers using the quant variant.

Zack (SDK): Will add TypeScript in one more commit. Quick TS example:
```ts
import { Redwood } from "@redwood/inference"
const client = new Redwood()
const resp = await client.generate({
  model: "redwood/mistral-7b",
  model_version: "2026-02-15",
  prompt: "Summarize the document",
  max_tokens: 256,
})
console.log(resp.output_text)
```

Sam (ML): Also request we tag the eval/regression set: `mistral-compat-2026q1` and add a line suggesting teams run the eval suite before pinning a quant variant. I'll add the eval link in the PR comment (internal link).

Ana (Docs): Perfect. I'll add a small "Migration checklist" with steps: 1) run eval set, 2) pin model_version, 3) validate latency on target infra, 4) enable fallback routing to `redwood/mistral-7b-compat` if issues. I'll leave the PR as draft until Zack and Sam approve. Merge after both approve. :thumbsup:

Zack (SDK): Coming in 5m with TS snippet and a short note about response_format changes.

Maria (Product): Thanks — please also add a short note in the release notes / release-notes channel when merged so customer success can prep messages for impacted customers.

Ana (Docs): Will do. Leaving TODOs in PR body for: attach CSV (Sam), add TS snippet (Zack), finalize benchmarks table (Ana), compatibility paragraph (Devon).
